pages.head: The Siege of the Sandbox
pages.html:
Sandcastle Knight

Pittsburgh, summer of 1995. Behind a brick house on a hill, past the tomato plants, sits a wooden sandbox. By day the kids build castles in it. By night, while the modem upstairs squeals and hisses, the castles belong to the toys.

Sir Grit is the smallest of them: a tin knight with a red plume, no taller than your thumb. He keeps four sandcastles and the toy chest he sleeps in.

This morning he woke to ruin. Lady Whiskerbane, the tabby from next door, has claimed the sandbox for her own. Her kneading paws flattened every tower. Ants dug into the keep, somebody left the hose running into the moat, crabs overran the tide pool and beetles hold the old burrow underneath it all.

Take up your shovel, Sir Grit. Rebuild the towers, raise the gates, and win back the Crown of the Sandbox from the cat who sleeps on it.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Installing

Copy every file on this disk into one directory on your hard disk, for example C:\SANDCAST, and type SANDCAST. You need a 286 or better with VGA graphics and 640K of memory. All sound comes from the PC speaker, so no sound card is needed.

The title screen

The game dials up THE -= S A N D B O X =- BBS on its own (don't worry, your phone bill is safe) and shows the logon screen. Press any key for the menu:

  • Play starts a new game in the sandbox.
  • Read Instructions and Read Storyline show messages from the BBS message base.
  • See Highest Scores lists the Knights of the Sandbox.

Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Sir Grit will show you around by himself.

Your goal

Win back four castles, one in each corner of the sandbox, then face the cat. Each castle you win sets you down in the next corner, so the sandbox itself shows how far you have come.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Keys

ArrowsWalk (the numeric keypad works too)
PPick up the thing you are standing on
SpaceFling a clod of sand (needs the shovel)
BThrow a splash of water (needs the bucket, and water in it)
F1Help
F2Status: score, hit points, lives, inventory and your sand
F4Sound effects on/off
F5 / F6Save / load a game
EscQuit to the menu

A joystick works as well: button 1 flings sand, button 2 throws water.

Thrown sand and water fly the way you last walked, so take a step toward a monster before you throw.

Counting your sand

Game-Maker's status screen (F2) calls your sand Money. Every scoop of sand you carry counts as one.

pages.head: Sand, Towers and Water
pages.html:
Sand

Sand is everything in this game. Pick it up by walking over a bucketful of wet sand. With the shovel, walk into a dune to dig it: two bites and it is gone, and you keep the sand.

Spend sand by walking into things:

  • Tower rings (a circle drawn in the sand, with a little flag stake): one sand builds the tower. Walk into it again to plant your flag.
  • Anthills: one sand plugs the hole for good.
  • Fords (water with wooden stakes): one sand fills a square of the moat.

Gates

A castle gate lifts when you have planted four flags. The gate of the lagoon wants three golden shells instead.

Water

Once you find the bucket, water balloons and the cat's water bowls fill it, three splashes at a time. Only water can flip a crab. And with the bucket in hand, walk into a dashed outline in the sand to pack a wall of wet sand right there. Crabs can't get past a wall.

pages.head: Things in the Sandbox
pages.html:

Things that move you

  • Hose currents carry you along. You can step out sideways, but nobody walks upstream.
  • Crumbly sand bridges fall into the water behind you. Keep walking!
  • Waves roll up the beach and push you back to shore.
  • The tidal flat floods every so often. Wait it out on a sandbar.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
CreatureNotes
AntsPour out of anthills and run at you. One bite each. A clod of sand stops them; a scoop of sand plugs the hill.
BeetlesPatrol in lines and squares. Armored, but a clod of sand flips them.
CrabsScuttle back and forth and pinch for as long as you stand there. Sand bounces off; only water flips them. Or wall them in.
Hose dropletsThe garden hose spits them across the sand. Time your crossing.
HairballsCoughed up by the cat. They roll after you.
Yarn ballsRoll from the scratching posts. Too tough for sand.
Lady WhiskerbaneSix blocks of sleeping tabby. Her paws guard the way to the crown. Splash a paw twice and she pulls it back.

pages.head: Tips: The First Castles
pages.html:
The Sandbox

Grab the shovel by the toy chest first. Anthill Keep is inside the ring of dunes: dig in.

1. Anthill Keep

There is more sand than you need. Plug the anthills near the towers before you build, and the ants will leave you alone.

2. Hosewater Moat

Two scoops of sand fill the south ford. The west bridge is free, but it only works once. The current on the east side takes you back out.

pages.head: Tips: Deeper In
pages.html:
3. Low Tide Lagoon

Pick up the bucket near the start. In the crab gullies, pack a wall on one side of the crossing while the crab is away. Cross the surf between waves, and grab the golden shells on the sandbars while the tide is out. If the flat floods, stand on a sandbar and wait.

4. Beetle Burrows

Three root doors and just enough acorns, plus one hidden behind a crack. Bring sand down with you for the ford over the underground stream.

5. Lady Whiskerbane

Fill up at the bowls, take a step toward a paw, and throw. Then do it again.

pages.head: Secrets
pages.html:
We won't tell you everything, but:

  • Not every little hole in the sandbox was dug by an ant. One of them dials a phone number.
  • Something in the courtyard of Anthill Keep leads very deep down, and back up again.
  • Cracked walls in the burrows are worth walking into.
  • Ride the hose's lazy loop in the southeast corner. Round and round.

THE -= S A N D B O X =- BBS was a real bulletin board in Pittsburgh, PA. This game is for everyone who ever logged on.

pages.head: Registering
pages.html:
This is Shareware

You may copy Sandcastle Knight and share it with friends, upload it to bulletin boards and put it in shareware libraries, as long as all the files stay together and unchanged.

If you enjoy it, please register for $10. Registered players get the next Sir Grit adventure on disk as soon as it is done, a printed map of the sandbox with every secret marked, and our thanks.

Send a check or money order (US funds) to:

Sandbox Software
P.O. Box 4215
Pittsburgh, PA 15213

Please include your name, your address and the disk size you want (3.5" or 5.25").
